newsitem.title: UK: Vickers firms on renewed bid speculation.
newsitem.headline: Vickers firms on renewed bid speculation.

text.p: Shares in Vickers Group Plc rose 4p to 211p on Monday following weekend press speculation that the company could be the target of a takeover bid by rival GKN Plc, dealers and market makers said.
"This is an old story that the papers pick up every so often. The companies usually deny there is anything to it but that doesn't stop the talk," one market maker said.

The Sunday Times newspaper reported GKN, which makes armoured vehicles as well as car components, might be interested in acquiring Vicker's Challenger tank business but would sell off its Rolls Royce motor cars and medical equipment divisions.
Last year GKN dismissed rumours it had its eye on Vickers. Analysts said although a GKN bid could not be entirely ruled out, any near-term approach seemed unlikely.
"There are a lot of problems in Vickers which GKN would have to take on," one analyst who wished to remain anonymous said.
"Given the state of their own business, I wouldn't think it likely they would want to take on more problems."
Another analyst described the Sunday Times story as "rubbish" noting that whenever Vickers share price fell, bid rumours surfaced.
"I just can't see it happen. It might make some sort of strategic sense, but certainly not business sense, not at the moment," the analyst, who also wished to remain anonymous said.
Vickers shares have underperformed the FTSE All Share index by around 32 percent over the past six months according to data from Reuters Securities 3000.
